messages.author: c48a384dbad0597c
messages.subject: MCEM for missing obs data
parts:
Hello,

I just started using NIMBLE, and find it very useful. I tried BUGS/JAGS/Stan but I think the use of MCMC samplers  inside R is a huge advantage. During the past week, I found that NIMBLE is much much faster than my own C++ MCMC algorithm - not surprising at all. Using NIMBLE compiler, I see the path way to make normal R codes faster via C++. I am also glad this is happening at Berkeley.

Reading the manual, the MCEM function came to my attention because I was struggling with the convergence problem of EM, very sensitive to the initial values. I started with the example in the NIMBLE manual and built a simple (but useful) model as follows. It estimates the values somewhat higher or lower than what I provided in the data. I wonder why this is the case.

More importantly, I would like to know how I can implement the model with missing obs. In the traditional EM, I use the obs matrix, which is just a scalar "phi" in my model below, to indicate whether there are missing values. 

I would appreciate any ideas or help.

Thank you very much.

Seongeun

# Model
bgModelCode <- nimbleCode({
x[1] ~ dnorm(mu_0, 1)
y[1] ~ dnorm(x[1], 1)
for(i in 2:t){
 
 x[i] ~ dnorm(phi*x[i-1] + d, 1)
y[i] ~ dnorm(x[i], 1)
 
}
phi ~ dnorm(1, .5)
d ~ dnorm(1, .5)
mu_0 ~ dnorm(1, .5)
})


# some made-up data, random walk with a drift 

t = 25; mu_0 = 1
x = rnorm(1 ,mu_0, 1)
y = rnorm(1, x, 1)
phi = 1; d = 1
for(i in 2:t){
x[i] = rnorm(1, phi*x[i-1] + d, 1) 
y[i] = rnorm(1, x[i], 1)
}

# Run MCEM to get params
myMCEM <- buildMCEM(model = rModel,
latentNodes = 'x',
burnIn = 100,
mcmcControl = list(adaptInterval = 10),
boxConstraints = list( list( c('phi', 'd', 'mu_0'),
limits = c(0, 100) ) ),
buffer = 1e-6)
res = myMCEM(maxit = 50, m1 = 250, m2 = 500)

> res
      phi         d      mu_0
0.9638035 1.5226775 0.6414609

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: MCEM for missing obs data
parts:
Thanks for the update.  I was just in the midst of responding to your previous message.

Thanks for this question and glad to hear NIMBLE looks useful for you.

I may not be following what you want to achieve.  It looks like you are treating all values of ‘x’ as missing, and that seems reasonable.  Do you want some values of x[i] to be missing and some to be observed?  MCEM is used in lots of fields with context-specific details, so I don’t know what you mean by “In the traditional EM, I use the obs matrix, which is just the scalar “phi”.”  To me phi looks like the autocorrelation of latent state dynamics.

In general in NIMBLE, any values of x[i] that are provided as NA will be treated as missing data.  For buildMCEM, the missing data nodes are provided via the latentNodes argument.  If you provide ‘x’, it will treat all of x as missing.  But if ‘x’ has been provided as non-NA data, I am not completely sure that would work; I’d have to check, which I will wait to do until I am sure what you want to do.  If you want to provide only some elements of x in the latentNodes argument, you could use rModel$expandNodeNames(‘x’) and then subset that vector as needed.

Does that help?  Otherwise can you say more clearly what you want to be missing data?

Perry

messages.subject: Re: MCEM for missing obs data
parts:
Hi Perry,


Thanks very much for your response.


I should have been more specific. Sorry about that.


x is the latent state variable in this simple state-space model and y is the observation since y was given as data. I was hoping to estimate params, phi and d, when “y” has some missing values (please note that as you can see,  in the current model y does not have missing values). But in general EM can estimate params when the "observation" (here y) has missing values for time steps. Unfortunately, I find EM is not stable for some times.


What I am trying to do at the end is to use the MCEM-estimated param values in Kalman smoother when there are missing values in "y".


Please let me know if there is still something that is not clear.


Thanks very much.


- Seongeun

messages.author: 0ef2647ddd7095d7
messages.subject: Re: MCEM for missing obs data
parts:
Hi Seongeun,

Thanks for the further explanation.  So you want to use MCEM to estimate phi, d, and mu_0 with some values of y missing.  I think it should work to provide missing values of y as NA and then include the names of those elements of y in the latentNodes argument to buildMCEM.  For example you might have latentNodes = c(rModel$expandNodeNames(‘x’), ‘y[10]’, ‘y[20]’), if y[10] and y[20] are the missing data nodes.  You might be able to extract the missing data nodes programmatically using rModel$getNodeNames(endOnly = TRUE), since those represent what we call “end” nodes (they have no stochastic dependencies).  Similarly you could identify the x nodes as rModel$getNodeNames(latentOnly = TRUE).  See help(modelBaseClass) for more options about querying the model.

I should mention we have an improved version of MCEM in a development branch, which provides more control over algorithm choices.    Let me know if you’d like to get involved as a beta tester for that!

Perry
